name: Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOT)
tagline: Open mapping for humanitarian response and development — mapping places home to one billion people
project_type: open mapping platform and humanitarian coordination network
communities_served: people in poverty or at risk of disaster
dependency_risks: heavy reliance on USAID funding (effectively severed from early 2025 due to US foreign aid cuts)

news_articles.headline: HOT receives Audacious Project funding to map one billion people

academic_citations: The evolution of humanitarian mapping within the OpenStreetMap community. Scientific Reports. 2021. https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-021-82404-z

policy_outcomes.description: HOT volunteer maps used by US Marine Corps for search and rescue in Haiti earthquake 2010
OpenStreetMap data contributed to 95% measles vaccination rate in DRC and 27% improvement in tracking patients during Ebola response in Sierra Leone
Missing Maps project (co-founded 2014) engaged 150,000+ mappers to pre-emptively map vulnerable communities for humanitarian preparedness

outcome_methodology: partner organisation reporting, field evaluations, vaccination and disease response tracking data
documented_limitations: data quality varies by region and volunteer density
sustainability concerns following US aid cuts 2025
fee-for-service model concentrated ~70% of budget on partner delivery vs community investment
governance_model: 501(c)(3) with voting membership, elected board, staff, and four regional Open Mapping Hubs
curation_criteria: Humanitarian and development mapping projects prioritised; Tasking Manager coordinates volunteer mapping tasks
contributor_governance: Voting members elect board; open volunteer contributor model via OpenStreetMap and Tasking Manager
community_ownership: Data published to OpenStreetMap (ODbL licence); tools open source under various licences
controversies: Heavy USAID dependency described as structural risk; aid cuts in 2025 created significant financial uncertainty
Criticism that ~8% community investment vs 70% fee-for-service delivery created imbalance in mission alignment
ai_involvement: fAIr — AI-assisted mapping tool developed by HOT using machine learning for feature detection from satellite imagery
